papers.title: A new premodel for bounded type Siegel disks of some transcendental entire functions
papers.summary:
In the 1980s, Douady and Sullivan conjectured that the Siegel disks of rational maps with degree at least two are Jordan domains. Based on the study of Blaschke models, this conjecture was settled by Zhang under the condition that the Siegel disks are of bounded type, and by Zakeri for a large number of transcendental entire functions under the same condition. The entire functions studied by Zakeri have exactly one finite asymptotic value, which is the center of the fixed Siegel disk. Chéritat, and later with Epstein, also studied the Siegel disk boundaries of such type transcendental entire functions by developing Ghys-like models.
  In this paper, by introducing a new premodel, we prove that the fixed bounded type Siegel disk centered at the non-zero point $λ-1$ of $f_λ(z)=e^{1-λ}ze^z$ is a quasi-disk whose boundary contains the critical point $-1$. The asymptotic value $0$ is not contained in the Siegel disk of these entire functions, which is essentially different from the previous results. Moreover, we prove that the Julia sets of these functions with a fixed bounded type Siegel disk are locally connected.

papers.title: Minimum degree thresholds for even cycle residues
papers.summary: Dean's conjecture asserts that, for every integer $m\ge3$, every graph of minimum degree at least $m$ has a cycle whose length is divisible by $m$. This degree bound is best possible for odd $m$. For every integer $k\ge2$, we prove that every graph of minimum degree at least $2k-1$ has a cycle whose length is congruent to $r$ modulo $2k$ for every even $r\not\equiv2\pmod{2k}$. Consequently, $2k-1$ is the sharp minimum degree threshold for a cycle whose length is divisible by $2k$. For bipartite graphs, we prove that minimum degree at least $k$ guarantees the same residue classes for every $k\ge4$, and we characterize their end-blocks when no cycle has length congruent to $2$ modulo $2k$. The bipartite degree bound is also sharp, and the exclusion of residue $2$ is necessary even for connected graphs of arbitrarily large order.

papers.title: Growth of Sobolev Norms for Linear Schrodinger Equations with Denjoy--Carleman Potentials
papers.summary:
We consider the linear Schrödinger equation on a torus of arbitrary dimension with a real time-dependent potential satisfying a mixed space--time Denjoy--Carleman condition. More precisely, for an increasing concave weight \(ω(r)\asymp \log^σ(e+r)\), \(σ> 1\),we assume \[
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|\partial_t^q\widehat V(k,t)|
  \le Ae^{Bq^{p}}e^{-ρ_{0}ω(|k|)},\qquad
  p=\fracσ{σ-1}. \] The corresponding spatial class is strictly larger than every Gevrey class, while the moment factor gives the quantitative ultradifferentiable control in time needed by the finite normal form. We adapt the method of Delort and Fang--Zhang to this non-power Fourier weight. The essential new point is a quantitative operator calculus whose majorant is built from the moment sequence and an auxiliary factorial that closes the exact Leibniz convolutions. For every $s>0$ we prove \[
  \|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C_s
  \exp\{C_s[\log(2+|t|)]^{\frac{1}σ}\}
  \|u(0)\|_{H^s}. \] The estimate is valid for every \(t\in\mathbb R\), holds in every space dimension, requires neither smallness, quasi-periodicity, nor a transversality condition.

papers.title: The Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture I: three-dimensional lattice polytopes
papers.summary: We prove the three-dimensional Zaks--Perles--Wills volume bound for lattice polytopes with $k\ge3$ interior lattice points: the Euclidean volume of such a lattice polytope is at most $6(k+1)$, with equality if and only if the polytope is affinely unimodularly equivalent to $\operatorname{conv}(0,2e_1,3e_2,6(k+1)e_3)$. The inequality is strict when the minimum lattice width is at least three. Together with the known cases $k=1,2$, this completely resolves the three-dimensional Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture.

papers.title: Efficient Nominal Automata Computation with Strong Nominal Sets
papers.summary: Nominal automata and register automata are expressively equivalent models of computation over infinite alphabets, yet an algorithmic gap separates them in practice: dedicated algorithms decide language equivalence of deterministic register automata in polynomial time by working orbit-wise, while general-purpose nominal-computation tools that rely on SMT solvers hide the orbit structure and degrade rapidly even on small instances. We trace this gap to non-trivial local symmetries in nominal sets and observe that the configuration spaces of register automata correspond to strong nominal sets, whose elements carry only trivial local symmetries. We characterize strong nominal sets categorically, consolidating known and new equivalences, and derive a constraint-free array representation of orbit-finite strong nominal sets and equivariant maps; we further prove the existence of projective covers, guaranteeing that every nominal set admits a strong approximation preserving both orbit count and dimensions, computable for quotients of strong nominal sets. Building on these results, we develop concrete algorithms for language equivalence, minimization, and active learning, bridging the algorithmic gap for equivalence (in polynomial time for a fixed alphabet dimension) and extending the orbit-wise approach to minimization and learning. Finally, our implementation Namae, based on the array representation, outperforms existing nominal-computation tools and, at scale, stays within a small constant factor of a dedicated register-automaton equivalence tool.

papers.title: A faster algorithm for commutator length in free groups
papers.summary: We compute the commutator length $\cl(w)$ of a reduced word $w\in[F,F]$ of length $M$ in a free group. Given a target $g\ge1$, a deterministic algorithm decides $\cl(w)\le g$ and, when it holds, returns a decomposition into at most $g$ commutators, in $O(M^{3g})$ steps; trying $g=1,2,\dots$ gives $\cl(w)$ in $O(M^{3\cl(w)})$ steps. For $g=1$ the same test takes $O(M)$ expected steps on a uniformly random reduced input in $[F,F]$. All bounds are in the unit-cost model.

papers.title: Between proper and strong edge-colorings of graphs with maximum degree at most four
papers.summary:
A $(1^j,2^k)$-packing edge-coloring of a graph $G$ is a partition of its edge set $E(G)$ into $j$ matchings and $k$ induced matchings. It can be viewed as intermediate colorings between proper and strong edge-coloring. The study of this topic on subcubic graphs has drawn considerable attention recently, with many conjectures and open problems proposed and resolved. However, very few results are known for graphs with maximum degree four or more. Henderson, Kennedy, and Santana showed that every graph with degree at most four has a $(1,2^{19})$-packing edge-coloring and a $(1^2,2^{17})$-packing edge-coloring.
  In this paper, we improve the results of Henderson, Kennedy, and Santana by showing every graph with degree at most four has a $(1,2^{17})$-packing edge-coloring. As a corollary of our result, every graph with degree at most four has a $(1^2,2^{16})$-packing edge-coloring.

papers.title: $H_2$-optimal riblet profiles for turbulence suppression in channel flows
papers.summary: The drag-reducing properties of streamwise-elongated surface corrugations, commonly referred to as riblets, have been extensively studied through experiments, simulations, and reduced-order modeling. Notably, the linearized Navier-Stokes framework introduced by Ran, Zare, and Jovanovic (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 906, 2021) employs volume penalization to model riblet-induced boundary conditions and predict drag reduction. These approaches typically quantify drag reduction as a function of a single geometric parameter, such as spanwise spacing or groove cross-sectional area, evaluated over fixed riblet shapes. As a result, identifying optimal riblet geometries across a broader design space often necessitates exhaustive parametric studies. To address this problem, we propose an optimization framework for the systematic design of optimal riblet shapes. Accordingly, we reformulate the volume penalization term in the linearized dynamics as a structured state-feedback operator. Targeting maximal suppression of turbulence, we pose a composite optimization problem that minimizes the steady-state variance of velocity fluctuations and riblet-induced dynamical augmentations while maintaining a constant bulk-flux. For a fixed spanwise wavelength (riblet spacing), this framework yields optimal wall-normal profiles that achieve maximal turbulence attenuation.

papers.title: An Explicit Construction of Large Families of MSTD Sets
papers.summary: A finite set $S\subset\mathbb Z$ is more sums than differences (MSTD) if $|S+S|>|S-S|$. Yufei Zhao's bidirectional-ballot construction gives $Θ(2^N/N)$ MSTD subsets of $[0,N-1]$, the best previously known size bound for an explicit family, to the author's knowledge. We improve this bound: for every fixed integer $T\geq1$, we construct a family of $Θ_T(2^N/(\log_2^{\circ T} N)^{2^T})$ MSTD subsets, where $\log_2^{\circ T}$ denotes the $T$-fold iterated logarithm. This family is asymptotically larger than Zhao's for every fixed $T\geq1$. A subfamily of the same order of magnitude can be numbered so that any chosen member can be generated deterministically in time polynomial in $N$, without listing preceding members. As a supplementary comparison, replacing the terminal ballot rule by exhaustive fringe search gives a positive-proportion family with the same polynomial-time generation property.

papers.title: More lower bounds for Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers
papers.summary: We give explicit colourings improving the comparison lower bounds assembled here for several Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers. The main algebraic tool generalises Rabung's power-residue colouring from arithmetic progressions to arbitrary sets. If every translate of a t-element set S in F_p meets at least two classes of the r-th power character, and the integer weights have both parities, then a period-2p one-weight colouring of [t]^p has no monochromatic combinatorial line. The 19 displayed algebraic certificates comprise 18 improvements and one closed-form reproduction; they include HJ(4,3)>=164, HJ(5,4)>=7418, and HJ(5,6)>=34034. The underlying period-p construction also proves kappa_ow(t,r)>=p-1 for the one-weight bracket ceiling, in particular kappa_ow(5,4)>=7416 and kappa_ow(5,6)>=34032. Warm breakout-weighted tabu search on the type simplex gives HJ(3,4)>=51. Whole-colouring local search gives W(8,3)>522, W(11,3)>1193, and W(17,3)>3620. All accepted certificates are available separately and are checked by direct enumeration; unresolved searches are reported as UNKNOWN, not UNSAT.

papers.title: Flocking Time and Graph Volume in Nonlinear Cucker-Smale Models with Dynamic Networks
papers.summary: This study proposes a Cucker-Smale model incorporating dynamic networks and the discrete $p$-Laplacian ($p \in (1,2)$) and analyzes the relationship between flocking time constraints and graph connectivity from both theoretical and experimental perspectives. We establish that this model achieves flocking within finite time and derive a quantitative relationship between the lower bound of flocking time and graph volume. Based on these results, we observe that imposing sufficiently small flocking time induces an increase in network volume, and that larger initial velocity variance requires greater volume under the same time constraint. In our experiments, we trained a transformer-based PPO policy to select network structures at each time step. Under the most stringent time constraint, the maximum average number of connections increased sharply, confirming a threshold effect. The negative correlation between convergence time and average number of connections reflects the theoretical results well. This study provides quantitative evidence for the phenomenon that time constraints induce connection mobilization.

papers.title: On Threshold Probabilities for the Stability of the Independence Number of a Random Subgraph
papers.summary: For an arbitrary sequence of graphs $G_n$, we consider a random spanning subgraph $G_{n,p}$ in which each edge of the graph $G_n$ survives independently of the others with probability $p$. We obtain a general upper bound for the independence number $α(G_{n,p})$, from which, for an arbitrary probability $p=p(n)$, we derive sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability, i.e., for the equality $α(G_{n,p})=(1+o(1))α(G_n)$ asymptotically almost surely, as well as upper bounds for the independence number of the random subgraph, including unconditional ones; for $p=1/2$ they recover A. M. Raigorodskii's results of 2017 and 2026. Under additional conditions on the structure of the independent sets of the graph $G_n$, we find, up to a constant factor, the threshold probabilities for both asymptotic and exact stability (the equality $α(G_{n,p})=α(G_n)$). Special cases include results on the graphs $G(n,r,<s)$ for growing $r$ and $s$, including Kneser graphs for growing $r$; we also give examples of complete multipartite graphs, graphs on the blocks of Steiner systems, and $q$-analogues of Kneser graphs.

papers.title: On Contractibility of Geometric Joins
papers.summary: The geometric join of a family of sets in $\mathbb R^d$ is the union of the convex hulls of all colorful sets. For every $d \geq 4$, we construct $\lceil\frac{(d-1)^2}{2}\rceil$ sets in $\mathbb R^d$ whose geometric join is not contractible, disproving the conjecture of Bárány, Holmsen, and Karasev that the geometric join of at least $d+1$ sets is contractible.

papers.title: The chromatic-AT choosability of Pseudo-Halin graphs
papers.summary: The \emph{Alon-Tarsi number} $AT(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that $G$ admits an orientation $D$ with maximum outdegree at most $k-1$ in which the number of even Eulerian subdigraphs differs from the number of odd Eulerian subdigraphs. A 2-connected planar graph $G$ with minimum degree at least 3 is called a \emph{pseudo-Halin graph} if deleting the edges on the boundary of a single face $f_0$ yields a tree. Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote the class of pseudo-Halin graphs in which no two interior vertices are adjacent and every interior vertex has odd degree (equivalently, graphs obtained by iterated Hajós sums of wheels with an odd number of exterior vertices). In this paper, we completely determine the chromatic number and the Alon-Tarsi number of all pseudo-Halin graphs. Specifically, by structural induction and the method of $AT$-orientations, we prove that $AT(G)=χ(G)=4$ if $G\in\mathcal{A}$, and $AT(G)=χ(G)=3$ otherwise. Consequently, every pseudo-Halin graph is chromatic-AT choosable.

papers.title: The topology of the mean action spectrum
papers.summary: We prove that if an area-preserving diffeomorphism of the closed two-disk is neither a pseudo-rotation nor a periodic map, then the closure of its mean action spectrum contains an interval of positive length. This partially answers a question of Hutchings. We do not require any additional assumptions on the area-preserving map, such as non-degeneracy or specific behavior near the boundary.

papers.title: Real-Rootedness and Log-Concavity of Zigzag Eulerian Polynomials
papers.summary: We prove that the zigzag Eulerian polynomials have only real, negative, simple zeros, and hence strictly log-concave coefficients, settling the first two parts of a conjecture of Petersen and Zhuang. Real-rootedness in combinatorics is usually proved inside a single algebraic framework, such as interlacing or stability. Our proof rests on a different premise: different parts of a zero set become visible in different representations of the same polynomial, and classical tools suffice once each part is viewed in the right one. The bridge between representations is a local rule. Forgetting the order in which a bounded-jump path visits positions leaves only a nearest-neighbor condition on sorted gaps, which makes an encoding via a transfer matrix much simpler to see. From there the argument passes to complex analysis. The sizes of the matrix's eigenmodes locate the zeros at the two ends of the negative axis, through Rouché's theorem. In a logarithmic coordinate the generating function becomes a combination of derivatives of the hyperbolic secant, akin to the classical derivative polynomials, and the arguments of its nearest poles produce a sine that fixes the signs between consecutive central zeros. The zeros are thus read off from the poles of an associated kernel. More broadly, the proof suggests that combinatorial polynomials defined by local constraints carry analytic structure, in their spectra and in the poles of their kernels, that is complementary to the usual algebraic methods and that classical complex analysis can exploit directly.

papers.title: Directed triangles in oriented graphs without a directed cycle of length $3t$
papers.summary: For integers $k,\ell\ge 3$, let $\operatorname{ex}(n,\Cdir_k,\Cdir_\ell)$ denote the maximum number of directed cycles of length $k$ in an $n$-vertex oriented graph containing no directed cycles of length $\ell$. Grzesik, Jaworska, Kielak, Kuc and Ślusarczyk~\cite{GJ} systematically studied the generalized Turán problem for directed cycles and conjectured that, for every fixed integer $t\ge 2$, $\operatorname{ex}(n,\Cdir_3,\Cdir_{3t})=\frac{t-1}{4}n^2+o(n^2)$. They proved this asymptotic formula for $t=2$. In this paper, we prove it for every fixed integer $t\ge 3$, thereby confirming the conjecture.

papers.title: Toroidal Obstructions with No K_5 Minor
papers.summary: Finding the complete set of forbidden minors for the torus remains an open problem. We determine the complete list of toroidal minor obstructions with no $K_5$ minor and prove that there are exactly $74$, each with between $10$ and $14$ vertices. Combined with the known classification of toroidal obstructions with no $K_{3,3}$ minor, this determines every toroidal obstruction that excludes one of the forbidden minors for planarity. The proof uses three-vertex cuts to show that, apart from $K_{3,7}$, every three-connected obstruction in this class has two distinct independent triples, each the common neighborhood of at least two degree-three vertices. The classification proceeds by considering the possible intersections of these triples and reduces each case by planarity tests and enumeration of the possible graph forms. From the $74$ minor obstructions we also obtain a complete list of $381$ topological obstructions for the torus with no $K_5$ minor.

papers.title: Enumerating orbits of finite classical groups on their Lie algebras
papers.summary: We enumerate the orbits of a finite classical group in the adjoint action on its Lie algebra, giving exact generating functions and very good upper bounds. We treat the general linear, unitary, symplectic and orthogonal groups, in both odd and even characteristic. In even characteristic, we get very nice formulas for the number of orbits on nilpotent classes both in the finite and algebraically closed case. We discuss the connection with commuting varieties.

papers.title: Star decomposition of complete multipartite graphs
papers.summary: We study minimum degree-sum conditions for decompositions into stars of sizes $k$ and $k+1$, where $k\ge3$. Write $σ(G)=\min_{uv\in E(G)}(d(u)+d(v))$, and let $c_k$ be the least integer threshold guaranteeing a $\{K_{1,k},K_{1,k+1}\}$-decomposition for every finite simple graph. Using Tarsi's sufficient condition, we prove that $K_n$ admits such a decomposition whenever $n\ge2k$. Together with the obstruction $K_{2k-1}$ of Zhao and Wu, this gives the optimal integer threshold $4k-3$ for complete graphs. For complete multipartite graphs, we establish the sufficiency of $σ(G)\ge9$ when $k=3$ by a finite computational verification and an extension argument. For every $k\ge3$, the complete tripartite graph $G_k=K_{k^2-k-1,k-2,1}$ satisfies $σ(G_k)=k^2-1$ and has no such decomposition. Consequently, $c_k\ge k^2$, even when the class is restricted to complete multipartite graphs. The optimal integer threshold in this class is therefore $9$ for $k=3$. Sufficiency of $σ(G)\ge k^2$ for complete multipartite graphs with $k\ge4$, and the exact values of $c_k$ for general graphs, remain open in this study.

papers.title: Positivity in symmetric webs and block permanents
papers.summary: We use symmetric webs to prove Marcus's block-permanent inequality for up to four blocks of every size, for five blocks of size at least three, and for any fixed number of blocks above an explicit logarithmic bound on the block size. The proof idea is easy: Bending strands in the Schur relation turns the comparison into a calculation with squared norms.

papers.title: Cubic graphs with circumference ratio 21/22 and cyclic connectivity 5
papers.summary: We construct a cyclically $5$-connected cubic graph of order $22m$ and circumference $21m$ for every $m\geq 3$. Consequently, the shortness coefficient of the class of cyclically $5$-connected cubic graphs is at most $21/22$, improving the previously known upper bound of $24/25$. We also demonstrate how I-reductions, which delete an edge and suppress its two end-vertices, can be used to prove cyclic connectivity.

papers.title: Klarner's sequences have density $0$
papers.summary: We prove that the set of non-negative integers $n$ which can be obtained from $0$ by repeated application of affine maps $x\mapsto 2x$, $x\mapsto 3x+2$ and $x\mapsto 6x+3$ has density $0$. Moreover, we reach the same conclusion for five other sequences of similar type introduced by D. Klarner. More generally, we establish a criterion excluding stationary measures with bounded density on the profinite group $\mathbb Z_P\cong\prod_{p\mid P}\mathbb Z_p$. A density-to-measure construction using invariant Banach limits and a combinatorial argument involving rational orbits and affine words yield our density-zero results. The criterion also applies to an infinite family of mixed-slope affine semigroups.

papers.title: FunSearch and Structured SAT Search for Weak Schur Partitions
papers.summary: The weak Schur problem asks how large an interval of consecutive integers can be partitioned into a fixed number of classes with no class containing a monochromatic solution to $a+b=c$ with $a\neq b$. We investigate whether FunSearch, an evolutionary program-search method guided by a large language model, can discover effective construction strategies for this classical combinatorial problem. In our adaptation, FunSearch evolves a priority function used by a fixed greedy solver, while a separate validity check enforces the weakly sum-free condition. This approach matches the known exact values for two, three, and four classes and reaches $WS(5)\geq195$. We then explore a complementary SAT-based approach. Guided by structural information from a 207-element construction communicated by Fred Rowley (Rowley, 2026), our SAT search produces and verifies a distinct valid five-class partition of $\{1,\ldots,207\}$. Thus the strongest construction obtained in this project reaches $WS(5)\geq207$, eleven integers beyond the best published lower bound of 196. The contrast between the two approaches also exposes a limitation of our FunSearch formulation: its greedy solver makes local, irreversible decisions, whereas SAT can enforce global structure across the whole partition.

papers.title: An improved bound on the strong chromatic index via local flag algebras
papers.summary: A strong edge coloring is an edge coloring where two edges receive different colors if they are incident or joined by a third edge. For a graph $G$, the strong chromatic index of $G$, denoted by $χ'_s(G)$, is the minimum number of colors needed for a strong edge coloring of $G$. In this paper, using a local flag algebra method, we prove that for every graph $G$ of sufficiently large maximum degree $Δ$, $χ'_s(G)\le 1.642Δ^2$, improving the previous best bound $1.73Δ^2$ due to Davey, Hurley, de Joannis de Verclos, Kang, and Volec.

papers.title: New necessary conditions on $h$-vectors of simplicial balls
papers.summary: Although the $h$-vectors of simplicial balls of dimension at most $4$ have been completely characterized, much less is known in dimensions $5$ and higher. We establish new necessary conditions on the $h$-vectors of simplicial balls in these dimensions. Together with the necessary conditions of Billera and Lee and the sufficient conditions of Kolins, our results yield a complete characterization of the $h$-vectors of $5$- and $6$-dimensional simplicial balls. We also give a characterization of $h$-vectors of simplicial balls of any dimension with neighborly boundary.

papers.title: Single-Vertex Metropolis on Minor-Free Graphs: A General EPTAS
papers.summary: We consider a class of combinatorial optimization problems where the goal is to find a largest induced subgraph with a prescribed property. We assume that the property is preserved by taking induced subgraphs and disjoint unions, holds for all edgeless graphs, and can be tested in polynomial time. We study the single-vertex Metropolis process for this class of problems. We show that on graphs excluding an arbitrary fixed minor $H$, this process is a randomized efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme. Starting from any feasible solution on a graph with $n$ vertices, it finds a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation within $\exp(O_H(\varepsilon^{-2})) n(n+\log(1/δ))$ steps with probability at least $1-δ$. This includes maximum independent set, maximum induced forest, maximum induced bipartite subgraph, and maximum induced subgraph of degree at most one. The proof uses improving exchanges on one fixed division of the input graph into regions. A recursive separator construction performs each exchange inside a region of size $r$ in at most $2r$ moves, with temporary loss $O_H(\sqrt r)$. We count move sequences through each transition and bound the probability of avoiding all near-optimal states. The general theorem bounds the number of Metropolis steps in terms of the temporary loss along improvement paths. We extend the result to bounded weight imbalance and give a weighted-star obstruction for unrestricted weights.

papers.title: Perfect matching complexes of antiprism graphs and independence complexes of generalized Petersen graphs $GP(n,2)$
papers.summary: We show that the perfect matching complexes of antiprism graphs and the independence complexes of the generalized Petersen graphs $GP(n, 2)$ are homotopy equivalent to wedges of spheres, and we determine the number and dimensions of the spheres. For the former we compute the initial values of Adamaszek's recursion for the independence complexes of cubes of cycles.

papers.title: Structural functional identifiability of unknown differential equation observation maps
papers.summary: In many differential equation models of real-world systems, the mechanistic structure of the dynamics is known, but the map from the dynamics to the observations is not. This is potentially problematic, as it can prevent us from e.g. learning model parameter values from data. Examples where this occurs include measuring a fluorescent marker as a proxy for the dynamics of a cellular circuit, and using wastewater measurements to follow the development of an epidemic. The nascent field of hybrid modelling, in which machine learning components (like neural networks) are embedded within mechanistic models, provides the tools to learn such maps. Here, the system's dynamics keep their mechanistic form, while a neural network represents the unknown observation map and is trained alongside any unknown core system parameters. This raises a question of identifiability: when can the true observation map be learnt, and when does one simply learn some map that transforms the dynamics into the available data? Building on previous work, we show how structural functional identifiability analysis can establish whether a model's unknown observation maps and core system parameters are identifiable, i.e. can be uniquely learnt from data. We both prove general results on when models with unknown observation maps are, and are not, identifiable, and demonstrate a general methodology (based on differential algebra) for assessing the identifiability of such models. This paves the way for applying classic differential equation workflows to the many real-world systems that contain such unknown maps.

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24982v1.title: p進フローの軌道：球体、時間1写像、極小群作用
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24982v1.summary: Zₚᵈ上の多項式または収束冪級数で与えられるベクトル場f（係数がp^cで割り切れる、p=2のときはc≥2）について、すべてのp進時間に対するフローが存在することを示す。写像t ↦ φ_t(x)が距離を正確に‖f(x)‖ₚ倍することを任意次元で証明し、明示的なフロー箱座標、衝突時間・回帰時間・軌道平均の閉公式、二次収束するNewton反復を与える。1次元では補間軌道が球体であるというMukhamedovの定理を回復する。さらに、係数ごとにp^cを法として恒等写像に合同な解析写像gが、そのようなベクトル場の時間1写像と正確に一致すること、およびベクトル場がg - idにp^{c+1}を法として合同であることを示す。これによりBellとPoonenの補間反復がこの種のフローであることが従い、定量的極小性判定法を得る：d個のそのような写像の変位g_i(x₀) - x₀がp^kZₚᵈを張るなら、それらが生成する群はx₀を中心とする半径p^{-k}の球体上で極小に作用する。CantatとJangの議論が開集合を含む軌道閉包を与えるのに対し、本結果は各レベルkおよび各次元でその球体を特定する。d=2かつk=1の場合、これはMarkoff曲面に対するJangの判定法であり、7830点で数値的に検証する。最後に、Gₘや楕円曲線の形式対数が明示的なベクトル場の整準座標であるため、vₚ(z) ≥ 1 + c（還元の核の深部）における局所的可除性vₚ([t]z) = vₚ(z) + vₚ(t)が計量恒等式のみから従う。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24982v1.appendix: 関連分野：arithmetic dynamics（p進力学系、preperiodic points、p-adic methods）とcomputer-assisted proofs and validated numerics（Newton反復の二次収束、数値検証）に関連。p進フロー、時間1写像、極小作用の定量的判定は、p進力学系における軌道構造の理解に寄与する。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22792v1.title: 演算子優先順位木オートマタ
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22792v1.summary: 本論文は、単語の統語構造の構築とその認識を分離する演算子優先順位木オートマタ（OPTA）を導入する。演算子優先順位（OP）行列が正準な木を定め、その木を正規な水平遷移言語を持つ有限ボトムアップオートマトンで評価する。OPTAは演算子優先順位言語をちょうど定義する。固定された行列と言語に対し、木文脈合同関係により、実効的に構成可能な正準完全決定的厳密認識器が得られ、これは垂直状態数に関して最小かつ同型を除いて一意である。非巡回OP行列に対しては、正準最小ランク付き木認識器の文脈遷移モノイドの非周期性によって均衡非計数性を特徴づける。既存のOP言語の特徴づけと組み合わせることで、非巡回行列に対しては、OP語上の一階定義可能性、Precedence-Oriented Temporal Logic（POTL）における定義可能性、およびスターフリー演算子優先順位表現との等価性が得られる。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22792v1.appendix: 関連分野：combinatorics on words（algorithms on words に関連）、equational theories of words and monoids（モノイドの非周期性・文脈合同関係に関連）。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22656v1.title: 実マークを持つGolomb定規：10マークまで実数最適値と整数最適値が一致する
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22656v1.summary: Golomb定規とは、任意の2点間の距離がすべて異なる整数マークの集合である。本論文ではマークを実数に拡張し、すべての差が1以上かつ任意の2つの差が1以上離れているという条件を課す。整数Golomb定規はこの条件を満たすため、nマークの実数Golomb定規の最小長G_R(n)は最適Golomb長G_Z(n)以下となる。すべての差の順序を固定すると実数問題は有限個の多面体チャンバーに分割される。これらのチャンバー上の分枝限定法と各葉での厳密な有理数証明により、n ≤ 10でG_R(n) = G_Z(n)が示される。各証明は1分未満で完了し、厳密算術のみを用いる独立したチェッカーで検証される。n ≤ 7については全チャンバー頂点の厳密な完全列挙により結果が確認され、最短実数定規が最適整数定規とその鏡像に限られることが示される。任意のnに対しn(√n−1)² ≤ G_R(n) ≤ G_Z(n)が成り立ち、したがってG_R(n) ~ G_Z(n) ~ n²である。非整数のチャンバー頂点はn = 7で初めて現れ、84個すべてが半整数である。この時点で80個が自身のチャンバーの最短点であり、40個は唯一の最短点であるが、大域的最適値は整数である。同種の12マークの例はSinger構成から得られる。一方、104マーク以下のすべてのSinger定規を最大ギャップで切断すると、自身のチャンバーの唯一の最短点となる。著者はこれをすべての素冪について予想している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22656v1.appendix: 関連分野：combinatorics on words（algorithms on words）、computer-assisted proofs and validated numerics（exhaustive search）に関連する。特に分枝限定法と厳密有理数証明による計算機援用証明、および完全列挙を用いた検証が本研究の中心的手法である。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22365v1.title: 群セルオートマトンの強推移性：特徴づけと決定可能性
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22365v1.summary: 本論文は、有限群アルファベット上のセルオートマトンであって大域写像が群準同型であるもの（群セルオートマトン）について、任意次元 d ≥ 1 で強推移性を研究する。強推移性とは、任意の空でない開集合から有限ステップで任意の点に到達できる性質である。非可換群上の群セルオートマトンは強推移的になり得ないことを示し、可換群上の場合はべき部分群による商を用いた分解を開発し、これが強推移性を保つことを示す。(ℤ/pℤ)ⁿ 上の線形セルオートマトンに対しては、Pontryagin 双対性を用いて、ローラン多項式行列 A の特性多項式 χ_A により強推移性を特徴づける：強推移的であるための必要十分条件は det(A) ≠ 0 かつ χ_A のどの既約因子も可逆な定数項を持たないことである。これらの結果を組み合わせ、任意次元で群セルオートマトンの強推移性が決定可能であることを導く。各固定次元 d に対し、群のサイズ N、近傍数 k、近傍半径 ϱ の多項式時間で動作する明示的な決定手続きを与える。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22365v1.appendix: 本研究は、興味ある分野のうち『cellular automata』（特に群セルオートマトンの力学系的性質）および『computer-assisted proofs and validated numerics』に関連する決定手続きの側面を持つ。また、線形セルオートマトンの代数的特徴づけは『symbolic dynamics』におけるシフト空間の構造とも間接的に関係する。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22364v1.title: ある種の超越整関数の有界型Siegel円板に対する新しいpremodel
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22364v1.summary: 1980年代にDouadyとSullivanは、次数2以上の有理関数のSiegel円板がJordan領域であると予想した。ZhangはSiegel円板が有界型である条件下でBlaschkeモデルを用いてこの予想を解決し、Zakeriは同条件下で多数の超越整関数について解決した。Zakeriが研究した整関数はちょうど1つの有限漸近値を持ち、それは固定Siegel円板の中心である。ChéritatとEpsteinはGhys型モデルを開発し、そのような超越整関数のSiegel円板境界を研究した。本論文では新しいpremodelを導入し、f_λ(z)=e^(1-λ)ze^zの非零中心λ-1を持つ固定有界型Siegel円板が、臨界点-1を境界に含むquasi-diskであることを証明する。漸近値0はこれらの整関数のSiegel円板に含まれず、これは先行結果と本質的に異なる。さらに、固定有界型Siegel円板を持つこれらの関数のJulia集合が局所連結であることを証明する。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22364v1.appendix: 複素一次元実力学系（Siegel円板、Julia集合、局所連結性）に関連する。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22365v1.conclusion: 任意次元の群セルオートマトン（GCA）の強推移性を完全に特徴づけ、判定可能にした論文。非可換群では強推移的にならず、可換群は冪部分群による分解で (Z/pZ)^n 上の線形CAに帰着し、特性多項式の既約因子の定数項が単元でないことで特徴づける。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22365v1.main_claims:
・定理2（3節）: 非可換有限群上の任意次元GCAは強推移的でも正拡大的でもない。よって強推移的GCAのアルファベットは可換。
・定理3と系1（4節）: 可換群G上のGCAは、冪部分群 G^m への制限と商 G/G^m 上のGCAがともに強推移的であることと同値。アルゴリズム1（PowerDecomp）で (Z/pZ)^n 上の成分に分解でき、全体の強推移性は全成分のそれと同値。
・定理6（5.4節）: F_p 上 n 次元、ローラン多項式行列 A を持つ線形CA FA が強推移的 ⇔ det(A) ≠ 0 かつ χA の任意のモニック既約因子 g について g(0) が L_p の単元でない（すなわち単項式でない）。
・系4・系5・定理7（6節）: 強推移性は全次元で判定可能。固定次元 d に対し群位数 N、近傍数 k、半径 ϱ の多項式時間（最大 log2 N 個の多変数多項式の因数分解コストを含む）。
・新規性: 非可換群での不可能性の全次元への拡張、冪部分群分解が強推移性を保つことの証明、Pontryagin双対と整閉整域上の行列の最終像の代数特徴づけを組み合わせた線形CAの判定条件、および明示的な多項式時間アルゴリズム。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22365v1.method_outline:
1. 強推移性を「全射性＋任意のシリンダーから単位元 e に到達可能」に言い換える（補題1、[13, Lemma 15]の一般化）。
2. 非可換群では、全射GCAの核が中心に含まれること（補題2、Garden of Eden定理を使用）から、中心外の値を持つ開集合が e に到達できず強推移性が破れる（定理2）。
3. 可換群では部分群 H による商と制限への分解（命題1）を示し、冪部分群 G^m に適用して定理3を得る。
4. 再帰分解アルゴリズム PowerDecomp により (Z/pZ)^n 成分に還元（系1）。
5. Pontryagin双対で、強推移性を双対準同型の単射性と無限可除元の自明性に翻訳（補題3〜6、定理4、系2）。
6. 整閉ネーター整域上の行列 M について、最終像 ∩ Im(M^k) が非自明 ⇔ χM が単元定数項を持つモニック既約因子を持つ（定理5）。これを A* に適用し定理6を得る。
7. 分解・行列計算・Berkowitz法・有限体上の多変数因数分解を組み合わせ、計算量を評価（定理7）。
既存の道具: Curtis–Hedlund–Lyndon定理、Garden of Eden定理、Pontryagin双対、Berkowitzの行列式アルゴリズム、Lenstraの因数分解。新しい部分: 冪部分群分解の強推移性保存、定理5の整閉整域版最終像特徴づけ、定理6の線形CA判定条件。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22365v1.research_connection:
・cellular automata / symbolic dynamics: GCAは G^{Z^d} 上のシフト commuting な群準同型であり、強推移性は位相力学系的性質。論文は群シフトやより一般のamenable群への拡張を open problem として明記（7節）。
・combinatorics on words / algorithms on words: 線形CAの局所規則はローラン多項式行列で表され、特性多項式の因数分解が判定の中心。多項式時間判定はアルゴリズム的側面。
・computer-assisted proofs and validated numerics: 判定アルゴリズムは明示的だが、因数分解の実装コスト評価が主で、区間演算やLean形式化には言及なし（推測）。
・arithmetic dynamics: 冪写像 g↦g^m による部分群分解は群的類似だが、p進的手法や arboreal Galois 表現への直接の言及は確認できず。
・aperiodic order: 群シフト・置換との関連は論文に明記なし（推測）。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22365v1.reading_guide:
前提知識: セルオートマトンの基礎（Curtis–Hedlund–Lyndon、シリンダー位相、Garden of Eden定理）、有限群論、可換環論（ネーター整閉整域、単元、モニック因子）、Pontryagin双対。
最初に読む: 定義1と補題1（強推移性のGCA的特徴づけ）、定理2（非可換の場合）、定理3と系1（分解）、定理6（線形CAの判定条件）。証明の核は5.3節の定理5。
精読範囲: 判定条件とその証明（2〜5節）は精読推奨。6節の計算量評価はアルゴリズム実装に関心がある場合のみ。7節のopen problemsは研究接続の確認に有用。
follow_up_questions: 定理6の条件「χA のモニック既約因子の定数項が単元でない」は、完全因数分解せずに判定できるか（7節のopen problem）。例えば終結式やグレブナー基底で単元定数項因子の存在を検出できるか。
冪部分群分解 PowerDecomp は非可換群には適用できないが、可換部分群や中心による分解で非可換の場合の別の特徴づけが得られるか。定理2は強推移性を完全に否定するが、部分群シフト上ではどうか。
定理5の整閉整域版最終像特徴づけは、L_p 以外の環（例えば Z 上の行列や p進環）にも適用でき、arithmetic dynamics の preperiodic 判定に使えるか。

papers.title: Proof Checking Continuous Reachability
papers.summary: This paper introduces a proof format and proof checker for certifying reachability computations of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) with polynomial vector fields. Establishing a proof checking framework for certifying ODE reachability is similar to the checking of UNSAT proofs for propositional satisfiability solving, but it is even more important due to the challenges inherent in dealing with ODEs, and even more challenging due to the numerical nature of ODE reachability algorithms. The proofs are expressed in differential dynamic logic (dL), and can be independently verified with symbolic theorem provers for dL (e.g. KeYmaeraX). Such proofs are naturally generated by reachability algorithms based on Taylor models, a popular technique to obtain rigorous bounds on approximations of ODEs. This paper proves the completeness of such proofs - if an approximation was correctly computed by some (possibly untrusted) reachability algorithm via Taylor models, then a corresponding proof in dL can be automatically generated and checked to be correct in dL's proof calculus. A dedicated proof checker is implemented in Lean4 for improved performance, which is capable of formally verifying benchmarks in the ARCH competition.

papers.title: On the monitorability of linear-time timed logics
papers.summary: In [10], we solved the monitorability problem for Tlin , a new expressive (linear-time) timed mu-calculus that we proposed. We showed that Tlin is strictly more expressive than MTL, the de facto timed extension of the well-known LTL. Moreover, we identified MTlin , the largest monitorable fragment of Tlin. The maximality of MTlin was proven modulo an expressive monitoring framework called Mon, yet under the assumption of reactivity. Our work in [10] was the first to solve the monitorability problem for such an expressive timed logic, and its theoretical results were accompanied with compilers (i) from MTL to Tlin and (ii) from Tlin formulae to monitors. This paper is an extension of [10] with the following new contributions. First, we generalise the maximality results to arbitrary monitors, which include both reactive and non-reactive monitors. Second, we extend the expressiveness results of Tlin . We completely revise the embedding of MTL into Tlin : we show that the syntax of MTL given in [10] was incomplete, and provide a new compiler from MTL, under its standard syntax with the strict Until operator and negation over arbitrary formulae, into Tlin . In passing, we demonstrate that Tlin is closed under complement and provide a fully syntactic complementation procedure. Moreover, we prove that Tlin is strictly more expressive than TPTL, a popular timed logic more expressive than MTL, and develop an automatic embedding from TPTL to Tlin . This gives Tlin and the machinery around it the power of a unified framework to reason on the monitorability of linear-time timed logics. Accordingly, we identify important monitorable fragments for both MTL and TPTL.

papers.title: Moduli of continuity preserved by the Hilbert Transform
papers.summary: It has long been known that the Hilbert transform preserves certain moduli of continuity such as Hölder continuity. In~\cite{GS01}, M. Goldstein and W. Schlag provided a criterion, based on two simple conditions, for a modulus of continuity to be preserved under the Hilbert transform. These conditions are not satisfied by the weak-Hölder and the log-Hölder moduli of continuity. More recently, A. Avila, Y. Last, M. Shamis and Q. Zhou proved in~\cite{ALSZ21} that for compactly supported $t$-log-Hölder continuous functions ($t>1$) their Hilbert transforms are at least $(t-1)$-log-Hölder continuous. A similar result holds for weak-Hölder continuous functions. In this note we extend these results to a class of continuous functions satisfying a couple of mild integrability conditions.

papers.title: Integer Programming Strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box Problem
papers.summary: We present a selection of Integer Programming (IP) strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box problem, which asks for the longest induced path in the $d$-dimensional hypercube. Current records are based on sophisticated, exhaustive searches, with optimality proven only for instances up to dimension 8, motivating our study of IP formulations. We address symmetries and potential strengthenings. With the smallest open instance having as few as 512 binary decision variables, the proposed IPs offer a challenging and intriguing combinatorial problem. In addition, we extend the problem to higher-dimensional grid graphs and provide solutions for unexplored and unsolved instances.

papers.title: Nilpotent skew-symmetric tridiagonal Bohemian matrices: a proof of Corless's conjecture
papers.summary: Corless studied the skew-symmetric tridiagonal matrices $T_m(u)$ with superdiagonal $u \in \{1, i\}^{m-1}$. He showed that $T_m(u)$ can be nilpotent only if $m = 2^K - 1$ and that the $2^{K-1}$ vectors $u$ obtained from the empty vector by repeated application of $u \mapsto (u, 1, i, \rev u)$ and $u \mapsto (u, i, 1, \rev u)$ give nilpotent matrices, and he conjectured that there are no others. We prove this conjecture. Reducing the characteristic polynomial modulo $4$ gives a necessary condition for nilpotency that is linear over $\F$. For $m > 1$ it forces $u = (v, 1, i, \rev v)$ or $u = (v, i, 1, \rev v)$, and an identity implicit in Corless's proof then reduces the problem to $v$. Since $T_m(u)$ is diagonally similar to a finite section of the Feinberg--Zee hopping matrix, the theorem also determines the nilpotent tridiagonal sign matrices. We further show that the $(1,1)$ entry of the resolvent of a nilpotent $T_m(u)$ is $λ^{-1} \pm λ^{-3} \pm λ^{-7} \pm \dots \pm λ^{-(2^K - 1)}$, with signs that determine $u$. The proof of the main theorem has been formalised in Lean~4.

papers.title: A note on Turán densities of daisies and hypergraph products
papers.summary:
The Turán density of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ is defined as $π(\mathcal{H})=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{H})/\binom{n}{r}$, where $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal H)$ denotes the largest number of edges in an $\mathcal H$-free $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. For integers $r\geq s\geq2$ and $t\geq s$, an $(r,s,t)$-daisy $\mathcal D_r(s,t)$ is the $r$-uniform hypergraph consisting of all unions of a fixed $(r-s)$-set with the $s$-subsets of a disjoint $t$-set. We show that for every fixed $s\geq3$, \[
  \lim_{r\rightarrow\infty}π(\mathcal D_r(s,t))=1-O_s(t^{-(s-1)}) \] as $t\rightarrow\infty$. This bound is best possible up to the implicit constant by a classical result of de Caen, and it answers, in a stronger form, a question of Ellis, Ivan and Leader, who asked for the case $s=3$. Moreover, we show a related result for matroid basis hypergraphs. We also consider Turán densities of hypergraph products, of which daisies are a special case. The product of two hypergraphs on disjoint vertex sets consists of all unions of an edge of the first with an edge of the second. For the product $\mathcal H^d$ of $d$ disjoint copies of a fixed $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ that is not $r$-partite, we show that $1-π(\mathcal H^d) \rightarrow 0$ exponentially fast as $d\rightarrow\infty$, and we determine the exponential rate in terms of the minimum number of edges in a homomorphic image of $\mathcal H$. This answers a question of Bollobás, Leader and Malvenuto up to a polynomial factor in $d$, and we further address a related question of theirs for products of two different hypergraphs.

papers.title: Leveraging Restrictions to Optimize Register Automata Learning
papers.summary:
Active automata learning algorithms, especially those that are able to learn extended finite state machines, such as register automata, can capture the behavior of complex systems and help analyses that uncover critical bugs in them. However, the performance and scalability of these algorithms often becomes an issue when models increase in size.
  $SL^λ$, the current state-of-the-art algorithm for learning register automata, uses a cost-efficient data structure with mechanisms for computing short and restricted tests. In this paper, we present $SL^λ_{=}$, an extension of $SL^λ$ for the theory of equality, which improves scalability by employing knowledge gained from prior tests at subsequent steps to restrict future tests to only those that are necessary to achieve progress in the next step.
  We have implemented $SL^λ_{=}$ as a new algorithm in RALib, and evaluate its performance by comparing it against $SL^{*}$ and $SL^λ$ on a series of benchmarks, including five widely used implementations of DTLS servers. Our evaluation shows that $SL^λ_{=}$ needs significantly fewer tests than $SL^{*}$ and $SL^λ$ to infer models of systems, and scales clearly better than them.

papers.title: Iterative constructions of semifields 2-dimensional over a nucleus
papers.summary: The construction of finite semifields dates back to Dickson's work in 1906. To the best of our knowledge, only two iterative constructions were previously known: those of Hiramine, Matsumoto and Oyama in 1987, and of Kantor and Williams in 2004. The latter yields, for suitable even orders, superpolynomially many pairwise non-isotopic semifields. In this paper, we use skew-polynomial rings to give a new iterative construction of finite semifields. This construction produces large families of pairwise non-isotopic semifields, each of which is $2$-dimensional over one of its nuclei. In particular, we show that this construction method yields semifields not contained in any family of semifields known so far.

papers.title: An Explicit Three-Dimensional Dispersing Billiard with Finite Horizon
papers.summary:
We construct an explicit three-dimensional periodic Lorentz gas whose
  quotient by the period lattice \(2\Z^3\) has 38 spherical scatterers
  with rational centers and four rational radii. The scatterers are
  strictly separated, so the associated dispersing billiard has no corners
  or cusps. We prove finite horizon by establishing a common blocking
  margin for every rational direction. A projected-lattice estimate for
  the face-centered cubic core leaves nine exceptional directions,
  handled by a finite line-space covering certificate. Simultaneous
  rational approximation transfers this margin to every direction and
  yields an explicit upper horizon bound. All finite calculations use exact
  arithmetic, with verification data and algorithms included. The positive
  separation and blocking margins also ensure stability under sufficiently
  small independent perturbations of the centers and radii.

papers.title: Formally Verified Semidefinite Programming
papers.summary: We present a formally verified Rust implementation of a first-order semidefinite programming solver, a nontrivial piece of numerical software. We wrote the solver by hand and then directed Claude to generate the entire verification in Verus, an automated theorem prover for Rust programs. We discuss the algorithm underlying the solver, its implementation in Rust, and our pragmatic approach to proving it correct in Verus.

papers.title: Convexity is overrated: Shortest paths on 4-polytopes are hard to compute
papers.summary: We prove that computing geodesic distance on the boundary of a rational convex $4$-polytope is NP-hard. We then construct rational $4$-polytopes with two rational points joined by exponentially many shortest paths of equal rational length, disproving several conjectures along the way. For the same problem, we also prove SQRTSUM-hardness under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions. By a separate argument, we show that the square of the geodesic distance between distinct rational boundary points of a rational convex polytope is a totally positive multiquadratic number.

papers.title: \textsc{Max-Cut} on Token Graphs
papers.summary: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with a positive weight assigned to each edge. A cut of $G$ is a partition of its vertices into two sets $X$ and $Y$; the weight of $(X,Y)$ is the sum of the weight of the edges of $G$ with one endpoint in $X$ and the other endpoint in $Y$. The Max-Cut problem asks for the maximum weight, $m(G)$, of a cut of $G$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, is the graph, $F_k(G)$, whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of vertices of $G$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. The phase-reconstruction problem for Heisenberg antiferromagnets in physics can be rephrased as a Max-Cut problem on token graphs. Motivated by this, we study the Max-Cut problem on token graphs, mainly when all edges are assigned the same weight. Our main focus is to bound $m(F_k(G))$ in terms of $m(G)$. We prove that $m(F_k(G))\geq\binom{n-2}{k-1}m(G)$, and that this bound is tight up to a multiplicative factor of $1+O(k/n)$; in the case when $k=c \cdot n$ for some constant $0 < c < 1$, we provide an example where this bound is off by a multiplicative constant factor. We also show bounds for $m(F_k(G))$ for various classes of graphs $G$. Finally, we consider the algorithmic complexity of finding $m(F_k(G))$, showing it to be NP-complete for a constant $k$, and giving evidence that, when the weights take finitely many values, it is not NP-hard for $k\geq n^δ$ for any constant $δ>0$.

papers.title: A refinement of Szemerédi's distinct-distance bound for points in general position
papers.summary: We prove that every collinear triple free set of $n\ge4$ points in the Euclidean plane determines at least $\lfloor n/3\rfloor+1$ distinct distances. This refines the classical bound $\lceil(n-1)/3\rceil$ of Szemerédi that is based on counting isosceles triangles. The refinement is based on treating the diameters separately: they only appear on the convex hull, so for them, we can use the planar diameter theorem and Altman's theorem on distances in convex polygons.

papers.title: New lower bounds for six small hypergraph Ramsey numbers
papers.summary: Let $R(k,l;t)$ denote the least $n$ such that every colouring of the $t$-subsets of an $n$-set with two colours has $k$ points all of whose $t$-subsets have the first colour, or $l$ points all of whose $t$-subsets have the second. We give explicit colourings proving $R(4,5;3)\ge 38$, $R(4,6;3)\ge 71$, $R(5,5;3)\ge 99$, $R(5,6;4)\ge 201$, $R(6,6;4)\ge 601$ and $R(6,6;5)\ge 84$. The first three improve the bounds 35, 63 and 88 listed in Radziszowski's dynamic survey. The last three improve the listed bounds 67, 133 and 72, and for the two 4-uniform numbers also the values 159 and 317 of a recent data deposit. The colourings of 3-subsets are invariant under groups of affine maps $x\mapsto ax+b$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n$, for $n=37$, 69 and 97, in the last two cases with one further fixed point. Those of 4-subsets live on the projective line over $\mathbb{F}_q$, for $q=199$ and $q=599$, and are invariant under $\mathrm{PSL}(2,q)$ or $\mathrm{PGL}(2,q)$, so each is given by a table of $q$ entries. For 5-subsets we show that, for every prime $q\ge 5$, invariance under $\mathrm{PGL}(2,q)$ forces six points all of whose 5-subsets have the same colour; our colouring is invariant under all affine maps of $\mathbb{Z}_{83}$. By known constructions the bounds give $R(5,5,5;3)\ge 9605$ and $R_k(5;3)\ge 98^{2^{k-2}}+1$, and $R(6,7;4)\ge 2001$, $R(7,7;4)\ge 12001$ and $R(8,8;4)\ge 588001$. The colourings, and programs that verify them, accompany the paper as ancillary files.

papers.title: Labeled Chip-Firing on Ordered Directed Graphs
papers.summary: We study labeled chip-firing on rooted directed graphs where for each vertex $v$, the children of $v$ are linearly ordered. When a vertex fires, the selected chips are sent to its children in increasing order. We show that homomorphisms preserving these child choices transport legal firing sequences. We then consider the directed lattice $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$ and ask which chips can reach a given vertex. We give a recurrence for the smallest reachable label when sufficiently many chips are present and show that consecutive pairing attains this minimum. Finally, we determine the largest reachable label by symmetry and prove that the reachable labels form an interval when the number of initial chips is sufficiently large.

papers.title: Rank and Rel in Strata of Abelian Differentials
papers.summary: We prove that every invariant subvariety M in a genus g stratum H(k_1,...,k_n) of Abelian differentials satisfies rank(M) <= rel(M) + 1 + sum_i (k_i - 1). In particular, every invariant subvariety with rel zero in a principal stratum is a Teichmüller curve. Combined with work of Eskin, Filip and Wright, this implies that each principal stratum contains only finitely many nonarithmetic Teichmüller curves. If rank(M) < g, we also show that rank(M) + rel(M) <= g - 1 + n/2.

papers.title: A Density Bound for Muñiz's List Reversal
papers.summary: Muñiz described the problem of reversing a list of positive integers under the following rules: given a list of distinct positive integers, at each step, one can combine two adjacent entries into their sum or break an entry into two entries with the same sum, under the constraints that after each step the list must contain distinct entries no larger than the original largest entry. The question of what lists are and are not reversible under these rules is studied and an asymptotic upper bound on the density of an irreversible list is established.

papers.title: Flatness and Tightness in Hypertopes
papers.summary: A hypertope is a thin, residually connected incidence geometry. For each pair of types $\{i,j\}$, the residues of that type must be polygons, and if all residues of that type are the same type of polygon, then we can record this information in a diagram $D$. Given such a diagram, we prove a lower bound on the number of chambers of a hypertope with that diagram. A hypertope that achieves this bound is called \emph{tight}. We prove that a hypertope is tight if and only if its diagram $D$ is a forest and, for every pair of types $\{i,j\}$ that is not an edge of $D$, every $i$-element is incident to every $j$-element. This generalizes a previously known result about abstract polytopes. Finally, we describe a combinatorial method and an algebraic method for constructing tight hypertopes.

papers.title: The Markov Property on Decorated Metric Planar Maps
papers.summary: We introduce decorated metric planar maps: planar maps whose edges $e$ are replaced by segments $[0,w_e]$, together with a continuous function on the resulting metric space, the decoration. We consider laws under which, conditionally on the metric map, the decoration follows a statistical physics model such as the Ising model or the Gaussian free field: the values at the vertices interact through a quadratic Hamiltonian and, given these values, the decoration along each edge is a Brownian bridge. Working with 4-regular maps with a boundary (the duals of quadrangulations with a boundary), we define a Markov property that allows explorations to stop in the middle of an edge. We show that, under mild regularity assumptions, the rerooting-invariant families of laws satisfying this Markov property are exactly the Boltzmann decorated metric maps. We also prove a strong Markov property and show that the random submaps inducing a Markovian decomposition are exactly the stopping maps for a suitable filtration. Finally, we obtain analogous results for classical decorated planar maps.

papers.title: On the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv problem for $\mathbb Z_n^3$
papers.summary: The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)$ is the least positive integer $t$ such that every sequence of $t$ elements of $\mathbb Z_n^r$ contains $n$ terms whose sum is zero. In this paper, we prove that $$\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^3)=9n+o(n)$$ for odd $n$. For every fixed $r\ge 4$, we also show that $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)\le\bigl(\binom{2r-1}{r}+1\bigr)n+o_r(n).$ Our approach combines Alon--Dubiner-type spectral expansion, Zakharov's convex-geometric framework, and restricted-sum ideas developed by Han and Ren.

papers.title: A census of alternating tangles
papers.summary: We give a census of the roughly 10 billion prime, connected, alternating tangles with at most 14 crossings. Along the way, we prove analogs of the Tait conjectures for alternating tangles and observe that aspects of the geometry of alternating tangles are reflected in their diagrams, as is the case with links.

papers.title: Near-Quadratic Sample Compression for All VC Classes
papers.summary:
The sample compression conjecture is a longstanding open problem in learning theory, originating in the work of Littlestone and Warmuth in the 1980s. At its heart is a connection between simplification and generalization: if a predictor consistent with a training sample is defined using only a small part of that sample, then it is likely to generalize. Sample compression schemes formalize this idea, and many natural learning algorithms can be analyzed this way.
  The sample compression conjecture of Floyd and Warmuth (1995) asserts that every binary concept class of VC dimension $d$ admits a sample compression scheme of size $O(d)$; a weaker conjecture asks only for size polynomial in $d$. Both have remained open: the first bound depending only on $d$, due to Moran and Yehudayoff (2016), is exponential in $d$. We prove the weaker conjecture by constructing a sample compression scheme of size $O(d^2 \log^2 d)$.

papers.title: Shadowing Property for Linear Operators on Banach Spaces
papers.summary: This note is dedicated to the study of the shadowing property for (bounded linear) operators on Banach spaces. We combine the spectral characterization of the shadowing property, recently established by Dragičević and Pituk, with tools from local spectral theory, to obtain new results and simpler proofs of known results on shadowing for operators. We also prove that the shadowing property always implies the average shadowing property and the asymptotic average shadowing property for invertible operators on Banach spaces. Furthermore, we investigate the shadowing property for some specific classes of operators, such as weighted composition operators and adjoints of multiplication operators on certain spaces of holomorphic functions.

papers.title: Mine Locally, Verify Globally: Exact Recovery, Compilation, and Distortion of Mined Temporal Rules
papers.summary: Specification mining extracts temporal rules that describe relationships between events in recorded system traces. Applying these rules in distributed monitoring systems is more difficult because observations come from different nodes, whose clocks may not be synchronized, and events may be lost or reordered during transmission. In this paper, we study how to aggregate the coverage of mined rules across observers, determine whether their temporal windows are needed during monitoring, and characterize their detection under event loss. Our evaluation uses IPv6 packet traces collected from 21 receivers across four continents. We show that local mining followed by global confirmation recovers centralized rule coverage under suitable conditions while substantially reducing communication overhead. In contrast, merging traces with unaligned clocks can distort coverage by introducing incorrect temporal matches. A window-gain criterion identifies rules that require temporal state, while our loss analysis and broker experiments demonstrate why contiguous losses can be more damaging than independent losses. The results identify separate requirements for aggregating observations, selecting monitor state, and handling event loss.

papers.title: Mateability of Fuchsian lattices with polynomials, and failure of algebraicity
papers.summary:
We prove that all Fuchsian lattices, with the possible exceptions of those associated with compact orbifolds of type (0,3) and (1,1), can be mated with complex polynomials, providing the first examples of such combinations beyond genus-zero orbifolds. We also present the first construction of matings between simply degenerate Kleinian groups and polynomial maps. These matings are realized as holomorphic, though not necessarily algebraic, correspondences, demonstrating that Fatou's vision of unifying Kleinian group actions and polynomial dynamics can be fulfilled in the wider setting of transcendental correspondences.
  We achieve this by generalizing the orbit equivalence mating framework introduced in our earlier work. Specifically, we use pinching and acceleration techniques to construct a new class of piecewise Möbius covering maps of the circle that are orbit equivalent to Fuchsian groups. By mating these circle coverings with polynomials, we construct degenerate polynomial-like maps whose analytic continuations yield the desired correspondences. The quality of this orbit equivalence plays a crucial role in the mating description, as well as in governing whether the resulting correspondences are algebraic.

papers.title: Pair Siegel-Veech constants for branched covers of tori and Veech surfaces
papers.summary: For a locus $\mathcal{E}$ of branched covers of tori satisfying a monodromy assumption, we show there exists an explicit constant $c_A(\mathcal{E})$ so that the number of pairs of saddle connections on surfaces in $\mathcal{E}$ of length at most $R$ and cross product at most $A$ grows like $c_A(\mathcal{E})R^2$ for every Diophantine surface in $\mathcal{E}$; this constant is moreover piecewise linear in $A$. In particular, this covers the case of billiards on rectangles with a barrier. Similar pointwise results are shown for Veech surfaces. The proof uses work of Margulis-Mohammadi on the quantitative inhomogeneous Oppenheim conjecture.

papers.title: The limits of inertia bounds on graph powers
papers.summary: We investigate the tightness of inertia and inertia-type bounds related to graph powers. This class of graphs appears in several contexts, such as the theory of distance-regular graphs, quantum information theory and coding theory. They are a priori not covered by previous separation constructions involving locally sparse graphs, see Kwan and Wigderson (2024), or Alon's pseudorandom graphs, see Elphick, Tang and Zhang (2025). Instead, we apply the latter's lower bound for complements of pseudorandom graphs to random graphs and random Cayley graph constructions, whose graph-power structure is ensured by additive combinatorial arguments. From this we are able to conclude that also for graph powers there can be a large gap between inertia bounds and the actual independence number. For the inertia-type bound, which is based on polynomials, we achieve even larger separation by considering sequences of graphs whose spectrum converges to a continuous distribution. Our methods draw from several areas of mathematics, ranging from additive combinatorics and probabilistic methods, to character sums over finite fields and arithmetic geometry.

papers.title: Divisibility of Character Values of Wreath Products of Symmetric Groups
papers.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group whose character table is integer-valued, and let $K$ be any fixed positive integer. We prove that almost every entry of the character table of the wreath product $G\wr S_N$ is divisible by $K$ as $N\to\infty$.

papers.title: On the Vertex Growth Rate of Integer Partition Polytopes and Their Non-Vertex Structure
papers.summary:
The Hardy-Ramanujan formula states that the asymptotic growth of the number of integer partitions of $n$ is $\exp(Θ(\sqrt{n}\,))$. We prove that the number of vertices of the integer partition polytope is bounded by $\exp\left(\mathcal{O}(\ln^2 n)\right)$. This implies that all partitions of $n$ can be generated from a negligible subset of vertex partitions using convex combinations.
  We also present new computational data on the structure of non-vertex partitions, which cause the huge gap between the number of vertices and the total number of partitions.

papers.title: List packing for graphs with small arboricity
papers.summary: We prove that every graph $G$ whose edge set is the union of $r$ forests has list packing number at most $2^r$. This means that for all $k\ge 2^r$ and every list-assignment $L$ with lists of size $k$, the graph $G$ admits $k$ disjoint proper $L$-colourings. While for large $r$ this bound is far from optimal, for $r\in\{1,2\}$ it is sharp. As a direct corollary of the case $r=2$, we obtain that every triangle-free planar graph has list packing number at most $4$, thus improving upon a result of Dvořák, Masařík, Musílek and Pangrác and providing the optimal answer to a question of Dvořák, Postle and Norin on (weighted) $ε$-flexibility of such graphs. As a corollary of the case $r=3$, we obtain a short alternative proof that every $K_5$-minor-free (and hence every planar) graph has list-packing number at most $8$, matching the state of the art. All results above also hold for the stronger notion of correspondence packing.

papers.title: A Model of Diverse Sampling from Language Models
papers.summary: Language models often produce high-quality individual samples but poor sets, with repeated samples clustering around the same semantic modes. We formalize diverse generation as sampling a size-$K$ subset of complete strings from a determinantal point process (DPP), where the likelihood encodes item quality, and the embedding geometry encodes repulsion between similar outputs. Exact inference over all strings is intractable, so we propose PoolDPP: draw a finite candidate pool from a tractable proposal, importance-weight the candidates toward the target quality, and run a $K$-DPP sampler on the induced pool kernel; a greedy MAP variant provides deterministic selection. We prove a finite-sample bound with an explicit constant: the KL divergence between the sampler's output and the target $K$-DPP decays as O(1/N) in the pool size. Empirically, PoolDPP extends the quality--diversity frontier on open-ended generation and the precision--recall frontier on ambiguous text-to-SQL (Ambrosia), and on mathematical reasoning (GSM8K), it raises diversity at about the same pass@$K$.

papers.title: The commutator subgroup of the Torelli group of a genus-three surface has finitely generated abelianization
papers.summary: We prove that the commutator subgroup of the Torelli group of a genus-three surface with at most one boundary component has finitely generated abelianization. The proof combines Gaifullin's finite-generation sufficient condition with the explicit generating set for the Torelli commutator subgroup due to Brendle, Margalit, and Putman.

papers.title: Isabelle Pool Server: a pooled verification service for prover training and multi-agent proving
papers.summary: Isabelle Pool Server (IPS), a verification service with a pool of warm headless Isabelle sessions behind an HTTP API, with session leasing and reclamation, memory-aware admission control, and a time budget on every call. Its verification interface spans single-step execution, block-level proof checking and whole-theory builds, with checkpoints for cheap branching and backtracking, and a build from scratch as the final arbiter. The service runs as a single container with monitoring and is accessible via a Python client, two MCP servers and a raw HTTP API. In our measurements IPS is level with PIDE MCP, a PIDE frontend for agents, at one worker and ahead of it at eight, at its commit of October 2026 (the tool is now PIDE AI). Once its sessions are up it scales to 32 concurrent workers on one host at 24 times the single-worker rate, and under memory pressure it refuses new sessions rather than losing existing ones. IPS is free software and publicly available at https://github.com/Deep-LCF/Isabelle-Pool-Server

papers.title: A Poisson boundary solution to Connes' bicentralizer conjecture and Kadison's problem on MASA
papers.summary: We prove that, for every inclusion $M\subset P$ of countably decomposable von Neumann algebras with a normal faithful conditional expectation, $M\subset c(P)$ has the weak Dixmier property, where $c(P)$ is the continuous core of $P$. By Haagerup's characterization, we have a completely new proof of Connes' bicentralizer conjecture, independent of the recent proof of Houdayer--Marrakchi. By Marrakchi's characterization, we also prove his relative bicentralizer conjecture. We also give a new solution to Kadison's problem after Popa and Marrakchi: further assuming that $M$ and $P$ have separable preduals and $M'\cap P=\mathcal Z(M)$, then there is a maximal abelian subalgebra of $M$ that is also maximal abelian in $P$. The proofs are based on a Poisson boundary theory for general von Neumann algebras, developed here as an extension of the theory of Das--Peterson for finite von Neumann algebras. Once this theory is established, the proofs for Connes' bicentralizer conjecture and Kadison's problem are short (around 7 pages each) and self-contained, relying only on results established by 1990. In both proofs, no separate treatment is needed for the type $\mathrm{III}_1$ case.

papers.title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
papers.summary: The Davenport constant $D(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence $S$ with terms from $G$ and with length $|S| \ge \ell$ has a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence. A long-standing conjecture, first proposed by van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk in 1969, states that $D(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$. We disprove this conjecture for every exponent $n=2k$ with $k\ge3$ odd. For each such $n$, we prove that $D(C_n^r)>r(n-1)+1$ for every $r\ge 8n-7$.

papers.title: On the Beauville Dimension of Finite Abelian Groups
papers.summary: Unmixed Beauville manifolds of general type are rigid quotients of products of compact complex curves of higher genus by free diagonal actions of finite groups. Their biholomorphism classes are encoded by equivalence classes of group-theoretic data. For a finite abelian group $G$, we characterize when these data exist and determine the unmixed Beauville dimension $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)$, the minimum dimension of such a manifold arising from a diagonal action of $G$. We prove that $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)<\infty$ if and only if $\exp(G)$ is odd and greater than $3$, and the largest invariant factor of $G$ occurs at least twice. In that case, \[ \mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)=\max\{\mathrm{rk}(G),\mathrm{rk}_3(G)+2\}. \] Specializing to $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)=2$ recovers the classical result of Bauer, Catanese and Grunewald: the finite abelian Beauville surface groups are precisely $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^2$ with $n>1$ and $\gcd(n,6)=1$. Although the Beauville dimension has a geometric origin, our proof is entirely group-theoretic and combinatorial.

papers.title: On the asymmetry polynomial of Schubert varieties
papers.summary:
Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group with length function $\ell$ and longest element $w_0$. For $w\in W$, let $P_w(q)$ be the Poincaré polynomial of the Schubert variety $X_w$. We introduce its asymmetry polynomial $D_w(q):=q^{\ell(w)}P_w(q^{-1})-P_w(q)$.
  Let $n\geq4$ and $W=S_n$ or $W(B_n)$. For $w\in W$ whose Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)$ satisfies $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=2$, we prove the sharp bound $[q^k]D_w(q)\leq[q^{k-1}]P_{w_0}(q)$ for $1\leq k<\ell(w)/2$.
  For every $n\geq3$ and $1\leq h\leq2n-4$, we construct an element $b=b_h^n\in W(B_n)$ with $P_{\mathrm{id},b}(q)=1+q^h$, and determine the asymmetry polynomial $D_b(q)$ and all Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials $P_{x,b}(q)$ for $x\leq b$.

papers.title: Minimal norm of regular vectors in the root lattice of a crystallographic root system
papers.summary: For a crystallographic root system $Φ$ with Weyl group $W$ and root lattice $L = \mathbb{Z}Φ$, we determine the minimum norm of a vector of $L$ having trivial stabilizer in $W$, and we prove that the vectors attaining it form a single orbit of $W$. Although this is a minimization of a quadratic function over the lattice points of a cone, the minimizer in the dominant chamber is always unique: it is $ρ+ λ$, where $ρ$ is the Weyl vector and $λ$ is $0$ or the minuscule weight in the class of $ρ$ modulo $L$. In particular, the optimal vector is the Weyl vector exactly when the Weyl vector lies in $L$. We give explicit formulas for the families $A_n$, $B_n$, $C_n$ and $D_n$, with elementary proofs, and the values for the exceptional types $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$. Finally, we explain the coincidences between the minimal norms by the folding of Dynkin diagrams.

papers.title: An Upper Bound on the Proportional Choice Number of a Graph
papers.summary: Proportional choosability is a list analogue of equitable coloring introduced in 2019 that imposes both upper and lower bounds on color class sizes based on the availability of each color. The proportional choice number of a graph $G$, denoted by $χ_{pc}(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $G$ is proportionally $k$-choosable. A recently proposed conjecture states that for any graph $G$ with at least one edge, $χ_{pc}(G) \leq Δ(G) + \text{col}(G) - 1$, where $Δ(G)$ is the maximum degree of $G$ and $\text{col}(G)$ is its coloring number. In this paper, we prove this conjecture using a generalization of Edmonds' matroid intersection theorem due to Aharoni and Berger, in which one of the matroids is replaced with an abstract simplicial complex. As a consequence, we can completely determine the proportional choice number of every path: $χ_{pc}(P_1)=1$, $χ_{pc}(P_n)=2$ for $2 \leq n \leq 5$, and $χ_{pc}(P_n)=3$ for $n \geq 6$. This resolves a question about paths that has remained open since the introduction of proportional choosability.

papers.title: A disproof of the El-Zahar--Erdős conjecture
papers.summary: El-Zahar and Erdős asked whether every graph of bounded clique number and sufficiently large chromatic number contains two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs, each of large chromatic number, with no edge between them. We give a negative answer even for triangle-free graphs. For every integer $g \ge 4$, we show by a probabilistic argument that there exist graphs of girth at least $g$ and arbitrarily large chromatic number in which any two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs that each require at least seven colors are joined by an edge.

papers.title: On a Secretary Problem with Two Equal-Sized Pools of Candidates
papers.summary: This paper presents the solution of a secretary type problem where the decision maker observes a sequence of offers of two types. There are N objects of both types and these objects appear to the decision maker in random order. Objects can only be compared when they are of the same type. The objects of a given type that have already appeared can be ranked according to a complete order. Objects of different types are not comparable. On the appearance of an object, the decision maker must decide whether to accept that object (and thus stop searching) or irrevocably reject it (and thus continue searching). The goal of the decision maker is to accept an object that is the best of its type. The authors present the general form of the optimal policy and the asymptotical solution. The authors give a strong result describing whether an object of relative rank one should be accepted when the same number of objects of both types have been seen.

papers.title: Proof-Relevant Interpolation for Circular Proofs in Linear Logic
papers.summary: First introduced for proving Craig's interpolation theorem, Maehara's method provides a constructive, proof-theoretic procedure for extracting interpolants in sequent calculus proofs. Building on this method, Saurin developed a ``proof-relevant'' interpolation theorem for first-order linear logic, in the sense that the interpolated proof is obtained by cut-introduction steps that can be reversed via cut-elimination. In this work, we extend Saurin's proof-relevant interpolation to linear logic proofs with cuts as well as to circular proofs in linear logic with fixed-points. We specifically show how Maehara's method can be extended in a proof-relevant way to work on non-cut-free and non-well-founded (but regular) proof objects, and guarantee that the interpolation procedure preserves strong validity. We also study conditions under which one can interpolate system L terms that are not necessarily in normal form.

papers.title: Balanced Simplicial Complexes for the $γ$-Vectors of Zig-Zag Eulerian Polynomials
papers.summary: In this paper, we construct a simplicial complex whose $f$-vector equals the $γ$-vector of the descent polynomial of an arbitrary canonically labeled rank-one poset. As an application, we prove Petersen and Zhuang's conjecture that the $γ$-vector of the normalized zig-zag Eulerian polynomial is the $f$-vector of a balanced simplicial complex.

papers.title: Meta-LSQ: A Closed-Form Sobolev Inner Solver for Few-Shot Meta-Learning
papers.summary: Gradient-based meta-learners such as model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) adapt to a new task with an inner loop of gradient descent that has to be differentiated through, and they meta-learn every network weight. Meta-LSQ instead fits each task with one regularised least-squares solve over a fixed random Fourier basis and meta-learns only three scalars, a bandwidth, a ridge and a derivative weight. Since the derivative of a sinusoid is again a sinusoid, the same solve can also take derivative observations, and the fitted model has exact closed-form derivatives of any order. On 10-shot sinusoid regression Meta-LSQ trains in 14 s and ends with a 5.5 times lower error than a first-order MAML baseline that trains 36 times longer, and a Gaussian-process control suggests that most of this gain comes from sharing one kernel across tasks. In simulated beam tuning at DESY's ARES facility with model derivatives it is slightly more accurate than an ALPaCA-style model and well ahead of gradient descent. Over DESY's full range of target beams, again in simulation and from measurements alone, its best setting has a median error of 7.3 $μ$m, against 14.4 for the published final beams of their reinforcement-learning agent, which has the lower median on their 300 trials of small targets. On real sensor-calibration data a learned prior mean puts it ahead of MAML on two of four targets, but an exact Gaussian process with the same change and an ALPaCA-style model stay more accurate on most targets, and it breaks down on non-smooth targets. On noiseless targets outside the span of the basis, in-sample criteria such as generalised cross-validation choose too small a ridge.

papers.title: The Lyapunov and uniform spectra
papers.summary: The \textit{Lyapunov spectrum} of a linear cocycle (or vector bundle) is the set of Lyapunov vectors with respect to all ergodic probability measures for the base topological dynamical system. This spectrum disregards trajectories that are atypical from the measure-theoretic viewpoint, and so it is in general insufficient to determine important properties of the cocycle, such as existence of dominated splittings. We resolve this deficiency by introducing a larger set which we call the \textit{uniform spectrum} of the cocycle. This definition is akin to Misiurewicz and Ziemian's rotation set. We prove several properties of the Lyapunov and uniform spectra, including relations between them. Motivated by a theorem of DeWitt and Gogolev, we consider Hölder-continuous cocycles over hyperbolic homeomorphisms and then provide bounds for the uniform spectrum in terms of the Lyapunov spectrum. We exhibit additional connections to the literature.

papers.title: The computational complexity of Undirected Vertex Geography with maximum height 3
papers.summary: The impartial game Undirected Vertex Geography is known to be polynomial time solvable. The variant in which vertices are assigned heights with maximum value m that reduce by 1 whenever the token is moved from that vertex, denoted UIRm, is known to be polynomial time solvable when m=2 and PSPACE-complete when m=4.
